claim_text: Pi is a documented exception to the name-matches-parent-directory rule: it lets a skill's name differ from its directory, holding that requirement suboptimal for skill directories shared across agent harnesses.
evidence_span: Pi allows skill names to differ from their parent directory even though the standard disallows it; that rule is suboptimal for shared skill directories used across multiple agent harnesses.

claim_text: Pi implements the Agent Skills standard leniently, warning about most violations while still loading the skill.
evidence_span: Pi implements the [Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.io/specification), warning about most violations but remaining lenient.

claim_text: Pi keeps only skill descriptions permanently in context and loads the full instructions on demand, the progressive-disclosure pattern the standard describes.
evidence_span: This is progressive disclosure: only descriptions are always in context, full instructions load on-demand.

claim_text: In the shared .agents/skills directories Pi ignores root .md files but discovers nested .md files inside grouping folders whenever they declare skill frontmatter.
evidence_span: In `~/.agents/skills/` and project `.agents/skills/`, root `.md` files are ignored, but nested `.md` files in grouping folders are discovered when they declare skill frontmatter

claim_text: Pi's agent is expected to load a matching SKILL.md itself with read or bash, but models do not always do so, which is why prompting or an explicit /skill:name command exists to force it.
evidence_span: When a task matches, the agent uses `read`, or `bash` when `read` is unavailable, to load the full SKILL.md (models don't always do this; use prompting or `/skill:name` to force it)

claim_text: When two Pi skill locations supply the same skill name, Pi warns and keeps the first one it found.
evidence_span: Name collisions (same name from different locations) warn and keep the first skill found.
